governanceNotes: D1 batch 51 (2026-09-24): deferred. Magnitude and wrong-target screens recorded 2026-09-24: a laryngocele is a rare saccular dilation of the laryngeal ventricle, and the located literature consists of case reports and small series describing presentation and management rather than condition-specific outcome cohorts; the nearest catalog-fit proposition located was a two-case report presenting laryngocele (one occurring after partial laryngectomy) and an epiglottic cyst as rare causes of obstructive sleep apnea (PMID 19288148), which concludes that upper-airway pathology can cause apnoea but supplies no quantified laryngocele-specific association, and the adjacent pharyngocele literature - including a case of bilateral pharyngocoeles attributed to high-pressure continuous positive airway pressure use (PMID 37663982) - concerns a different entity and would be a wrong-target attribution. A single case describing a rare cause does not meet this program's condition-specific evidence threshold, so no edge is authored rather than a one-citation draft that would raise the citation packet's quarantined-single-citation warning count.

Direction and constitutive screens recorded 2026-09-24: secondary laryngoceles are documented as arising from laryngeal tumour obstruction of the saccular orifice or from sustained raised intralaryngeal pressure, so a laryngocele-to-laryngeal-cancer edge would invert the established direction (direction-inversion guard); dysphonia, dysphagia, stridor, and neck swelling are manifestations of the lesion itself rather than distinct catalog secondaries (constitutive and symptom-identity guards); and no condition-specific laryngocele quantification of airway obstruction, respiratory failure, or aspiration was located, with no catalog identity existing for airway obstruction or respiratory failure. Reopening condition: a condition-specific laryngocele cohort or series quantifying a distinct catalog secondary, or the creation of an airway-obstruction identity that such a proposition could target.
